idea: SlowCook is a NEAR memecoin launchpad where being first is worthless. On bonding curves the first buyer pays the least, so sniper bots buy in block 0 and bundlers take a third of supply, then dump on retail. SlowCook replaces the race with a sealed-bid, uniform-price auction: bidders commit sha256(launch, bidder, price tick, qty, salt) with a deposit, reveal after the window, and finalize walks 64 price ticks to one clearing price that every winner pays, even those who bid 7x higher. Unsold supply is never minted (burned); LP and creator shares scale with what actually sold, so the pool is always seeded at exactly the clearing price. After launch a Floor Keeper treasury defends that price: a Uniswap-v2-style time-weighted accumulator, poke() intervals, and defend() buys back and burns only when the TWAP and spot are below clearing minus 10% for k intervals, at most 10% of the treasury per epoch and never above clearing. Creator tokens unlock only after the price holds at or above clearing. Evidence: 51 unit tests covering every error code, 1000-case property tests of supply/payment/solvency invariants, exact parity between a TypeScript model and the contract on 1000 auctions, real-wasm sandbox tests, and two live NEAR testnet launches with tx links. Live demo: https://web-omega-dun-65.vercel.app. SIMULATED: with the same 200 wallets, insiders' share of supply falls from 40% to 11% and their dump ROI from +437% to -9%. NEAR: NEP-141 token per launch via a sub-account factory, global contracts (measured), promises with failure callbacks, ft_transfer_call, NEP-297 events, near-connect. Limits we state: deposits are public, sybils can't be stopped (only made pointless), the treasury slows a sell-off but can't stop one, testnet only.
